questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Office life and how people make spaces their own
How to find a job with better working hours
Why hairdressers are happier than office workers
How to stop colleagues from stealing your things
questions.why: They look at life in the modern office, including research into objects people use to mark their workspace.

questions.q: Why is Neil annoyed at the start of the programme?
options: Sam has taken his favourite pen from his desk
He has to work longer hours than before
His pen and mug have gone missing
The office printer has stopped working again
questions.why: His pen and coffee mug are missing, and he blames people's behaviour since they started hot-desking.

questions.q: What did Neil like about working from home during the pandemic?
options: He could spend more time with his colleagues
He earned more money for fewer hours
He had a bigger desk than in the office
No early mornings and no crowded trains
questions.why: Neil says he loved it – 'no early mornings, no crowded trains… and no-one using my pens!'

questions.q: Why might a worker put home-made biscuits at the end of their desk?
options: To sell them to colleagues for money
To help start conversations
To stop people sitting at their desk
Because the office has no kitchen
questions.why: Neil says cakes and biscuits allow people to grab a biscuit and start a conversation.

questions.q: What did one young woman in Harriet Shortt's research do?
options: She carried a roll of photos to each desk
Painted her own desk in bright colours
She refused to work at any desk but her own
Asked her manager for a private office
questions.why: She made a montage on a strip of cardboard, rolled it up daily and pinned it up at whatever desk she used.

questions.q: What does Harriet think this woman's behaviour shows?
options: Young workers don't like working in offices
Hot-desking makes people work much harder
Most people prefer working from home
People want comfort and familiarity at work
questions.why: She says there's evidence people want to feel comfort, settled and 'have some sense of familiarity'.

questions.q: What did a hairdresser show Harriet?
options: A photo of her very favourite customer
A new chair she had bought for the salon
A curved mark worn into the floor
A stain on the wall from hair colour
questions.why: It was a half-moon scuff mark round the back of the chair where she had worn out the floor.

questions.q: What did the mark on the floor mean to the hairdresser?
options: That the salon needed to be repaired
That she had worked hard for many years
That she should buy more comfortable shoes
That the salon had too many customers
questions.why: She said, 'This is me… It represents hard graft' – meaning hard work.
